doc.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995

title: Club Plantation in St. Louis, softball and Williams's injury
summary: They recall the Club Plantation and George Hudson's band, morning softball games, and Terry carrying the injured Williams to his car.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: I remember you playing in St. Louis years ago.
Ah, I’ll never forget it.
And, what’s that club?
Club Plantation.
Club Plantation. With Hudson’s band, wasn’t it?
Yeah.
George Hudson.
You came through there with Gerald Wilson’s band I think.
I came through with Gerals Wilson. With Ella Fitzgerald.
We used to play softball in the park every morning. We’d get off at like four or five o’clock in the morning —
I wasn’t in shape.
Yeah, you were in shape. You were hitting home runs until you —
Pulled a muscle.
— made a mistake at the plate, and relatively speaking about the size that we are now, he was about that much more bigger than me. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
I wasn’t that much bigger.
I mean we were both smaller, but you were heavier than I was. I was about 130, 125.
You were?
Yeah.
I didn’t realize you were that small.
I was thin enough to ride a rooster. And, I don’t know is that the story you were about to tell? When you swung at the plate and swung the ball at the plate and missed.
And crumpled up at the plate.
And I picked him up and carried him.
In his arms. And carried me to his car.
I thought about that Father Flanagan thing.

Yeah. He ain’t my brother — no, he ain’t my brother, he’s just heavy. Yeah, and then took me to call the doctor, and the doctor came and taped me up and I went on back to work that afternoon. I mean no, I went back to work that night.
Yeah. We’ve been brothers ever since. But we were tight long before that even.
